title: The Monarch Butterfly
seo_title: Butterfly Charcuterie Board: Monarch Showpiece & What to Buy
description: A monarch butterfly charcuterie board for 12 to 15: mirrored wings of orange cheddar, mango, prosciutto and bresaola, with black olive veins and a baguette body.
hook: A giant monarch landing on the table, its wings perfectly mirrored in orange cheddar, mango and dark bresaola, with black veins you can see from across the room.

items.name: Wedges of aged Gouda or Manchego

why: Getting both wings to match is the hard part of any symmetrical board, and this one solves it with a folded paper template: draw half, cut it, and both sides come out identical.

Lines of black olives and charcoal crackers divide each wing into panels of orange cheddar, apricots, mango, prosciutto, bresaola and chorizo, and mozzarella pearls make the white spots along the edges. A long baguette is the body. It's a striking board for spring parties, showers and garden birthdays.

timeline.what: Draw and cut the half-butterfly template, slice the cheeses, and slice the black olives.
Lay the template, outline the wings and lay the veins.
Place the baguette body, fill the panels and add the white spots.

faq.q: How do you make a butterfly charcuterie board?
faq.a: Use a folded paper template to outline two matching wings in black olive slices, divide them into panels with olive and charcoal-cracker veins, fill the panels with orange cheese, fruit and meats, and add white mozzarella spots. A baguette makes the body.

faq.q: What makes it look like a monarch?
faq.a: The colors: bright orange panels divided by black veins, with white mozzarella spots along the edges.

Cut the template and slice the cheese the day before. Build the wings about 90 minutes before the party. Keep meat, cheese and cut fruit out no more than 2 hours, or 1 hour above 90°F. For a long party, build half, keep the refill in the fridge and top it up halfway through.
